newsitem.title: USA: Most stock index futures end sluggish day lower.
newsitem.headline: Most stock index futures end sluggish day lower.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures took back more of their recent gains and ended moderately to sharply lower in what one trader called "squirrelly" trade.
Traders cited profit-taking from recent gains and a dismal Treasury bond performance.
June Standard and Poor's 500 futures spent the day in choppy trade in lower territory, extending losses to hit new session lows after Treasury bond futures closed.
June S&P 500s erased virtually all of their Monday rally, a day when June sailed to a fresh record high. Traders said the market had rallied too far, too fast.
"To me it looks like it's a time out," said Greg Nie, technical analyst with Everen Securities. "It's just a down day within the context of the overall rally."
Nie said the run to record levels came so quickly that June had not had time to build support. When prices began to erode on Wednesday's profit-taking, June sank quickly back below the 820.00 level.
"On the break it was pretty much straight down," an S&P 500 floor source said. "But it wasn't as busy as yesterday. When it trades down in whole handles like that, there isn't too much action."
June hit a session low of 816.00 late in the day.

Trade was choppy in the afternoon before June S&Ps headed sharply lower. June S&Ps languished along with Treasury bond weakness and sank toward the day's lows after a disappointing 10-year note auction.
But soon after, June cut its losses on the sentiment that the Fed's Beige Book report on the economy showed subdued price pressures.
Treasury sold $12 billion in 10-year notes at an average yield of 6.74 percent, a bid-to-cover ratio of 1.86 and non-competitive bids at $383 million.
"We had difficulty sustaining above that 20,000 level," the trader said.

At the close, June S&P 500s fell 17.20 points to 817.65, Midcap 400s fell 3.35 to 266.70, Russell lost 2.30 to 361.60, Value Lines lost 8.30 to 724.20, NYSE Composite lost 8.25 pts to 426.00, Nasdaq fell 10.75 points to 913.75, and Nikkei 225 fell 220.0 to 19,905.0.
